expectations.text: Output warns that a single Louvain run reflects modularity DEGENERACY — many qualitatively different partitions have near-equal modularity (Good et al.) — not just random stochasticity
expectations.evidence: Section 1 explicitly states: 'The modularity landscape for any non-trivial network contains an exponential number of near-optimal partitions that are structurally very different from one another. A single Louvain run returns one of these almost arbitrarily... This is not random noise — it is a mathematical property of the objective.' Cites Good, De Montjoye & Clauset 2010 by name.

expectations.text: Output frames stability analysis as a PREREQUISITE before naming or interpreting communities, not as an optional improvement step
expectations.evidence: Section heading reads '2. Stability analysis is a prerequisite, not an optional step' and the body states 'Do not name or describe communities until you have established that the partition is stable.' The final section '6. Summary of the recommended order of operations' places stability first in a numbered sequence before interpretation.

expectations.text: Output recommends running community detection many times (e.g., 100+ runs) and measuring pairwise stability with ARI, NMI, or similar
expectations.evidence: Response recommends running Louvain 200 times with different seeds, provides Python code computing pairwise adjusted_rand_score and normalized_mutual_info_score across all pairs, and gives interpretation thresholds (e.g., Mean ARI > 0.9 = very stable).

expectations.text: Output recommends comparing Q = 0.67 against a configuration-model null (random graphs with the same degree sequence) rather than accepting it at face value
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section '3. Compare Q against a configuration-model null' provides code using nx.configuration_model to preserve degree sequence, runs 100 null graphs, computes Z-score, and gives a concrete example: 'If null Q is 0.55, your 0.67 represents a real signal above chance. If null Q is 0.63, the difference is marginal.'

expectations.text: Output mentions Louvain resolution limit or the alternative of SBM (Stochastic Block Model) for more principled partitioning
expectations.evidence: Section '4. Resolution limit check' explicitly states: 'With 4,800 edges, Louvain's resolution limit is approximately √(2 × 4800) ≈ 98 internal edges per community.' Section '5. Consider the Stochastic Block Model as a more principled alternative' recommends graph-tool's nested SBM with code and lists its advantages (generative, MDL-based K selection, resists overfitting).
